target.title: fix(imessage): recognize bare hex group chat identifiers as chat targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #89235.

Bare 32-character hexadecimal iMessage group identifiers were falling through to phone-number normalization in both direct-send parsing and cron/announce delivery. A real group identifier could therefore become a bogus E.164 target instead of using the existing `imsg send --chat-identifier` path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The identifier shape is produced by `imsg` for group chats, but it has no explicit `chat_identifier:` prefix. The final implementation gives that exact bounded shape one plugin-owned normalizer shared by delivery normalization, target parsing, explicit-target detection, and peer-kind inference. Service-prefixed identifiers use the same canonical path; invalid length or non-hex values retain existing handle behavior.

## User Impact

iMessage group sends addressed by a bare database identifier now reach the intended conversation instead of being normalized into a nonexistent phone number. Existing explicit chat identifiers, phone handles, and email handles are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased PR head: `d26dfb57e53e08bb0efd8c74e0191122abb857e7`.
- Focused behavior proof: 129 tests passed (55 cron tests and 74 iMessage tests), including lower/upper-case identifiers, service prefixes, all-digit hex, wrong lengths, non-hex values, parser inference, and the existing chat-identifier send path.
- Live local `imsg` 0.12.1 database shape audit: 500 chats inspected; 31 group chats; 20 bare 32-hex group identifiers; zero bare 32-hex direct chats. Only aggregate counts were recorded, and no external message was sent to a private conversation.
- Final structured autoreview: clean, 0.98 correctness confidence.
- Screenshots are not useful for this nonvisual target-routing fix; proof is at the identifier, parser, and send-path boundaries.

CI is running on the exact head above and will be required green before merge.
